value: MWCC emits the sign-extension (extsh/extsb) before a narrowing store ONLY when the stored value transits an INT-TYPED VARIABLE and is narrowed by a cast at the store. It does NOT emit it when the narrowing cast is applied directly to a float-conversion expression, and it does NOT emit it when the value transits a NARROW-typed (s16/s8) local. Canonical proof pair, both inside fn_8005C1DC and 0x50 bytes apart in the same object, so compiler flags/alignment are held constant: `*(s16*)&item->data[0] = (s16)k;` (k an s32 local) compiles to `extsh r0,rK; sth r0,220(r31)` in BOTH target and ours, while `*(s16*)&item->data[2] = (s16)(lbl_80346F6C * power);` compiled to `lwz; sth` in ours against the target's `lwz; extsh; sth`. Rewriting the second as `k = (s32)(lbl_80346F6C * power); *(s16*)&item->data[2] = (s16)k;` made the whole 0x684-0x6a4 window byte-identical. The narrow-local form is the measured-dead third case: fn_800606FC already declared `s16 wob; wob = (s16)(<float expr>); *(s16*)&it->data[8] = wob;` and emitted NO extsh; changing only the declaration to `s32 wob` plus a `(s16)` cast at the store landed the extsh and moved real 1356->1343.
